text:
sam_customer: Hey team — running into SSE streaming issues. Client receives partial output, then mid-stream we get a 429 and the client reconnects. After reconnect we see duplicated token accounting on our billing. Repro steps below, can you advise?

sam_customer: Repro (minimal):
```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-std', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` }
});
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = (e) => { // client reconnects here
  // client reopens EventSource with same TOKEN
}
```

sam_customer: Attached snippet from client log: 
```
event: data
data: {"chunk":"...partial text..."}

event: error
data: {"type":"rate_limit","code":429,"message":"quota exceeded mid_stream","request_id":"req_0A1B2C"}

// client reconnects immediately with same Authorization token, new connection id: conn_17
```

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the full request_id and the customer token prefix (just first 8 chars) so we can correlate on our side? Also, is this hosted or dedicated account?

sam_customer: hosted account. token prefix: ghp4f8a9. request_id: req_0A1B2C. Happened Friday ~15:12 UTC across 3 users, all using the same app token.

maria_eng: Noted. Quick hypothesis: our streaming meter counts tokens per active connection start + per-completed stream. If the upstream connection hits a 429 mid-stream and client immediately reconnects with the same token while our backend hasn't garbage-collected the old session, it may count both the partial session and the new session toward quota. That can look like duplicate accounting.

maria_eng: Can you also share server-side response headers from the 429 (if any)? we look for X-RateLimit-Reset / X-Client-Session or X-Request-ID.

sam_customer: Header dump: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 15:12:42 GMT
X-Request-ID: req_0A1B2C
X-RateLimit-Limit: 50000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000
Content-Type: text/event-stream
```

sam_customer: We also see an internal metric from our app: tokens_sent_before_429 = 432; after reconnect and resume we sent another 120 tokens and then connection closed cleanly. Billing shows ~552 tokens twice (counts look doubled).

maria_eng: Thanks. Two things to investigate server-side: 1) whether partial session accounting finalization happens on connection close or when stream reaches EOS; 2) whether reconnects with the same Authorization token within N seconds are merged or counted separately. I'll ask infra to grep logs for req_0A1B2C and conn_17.

rate-limit-bot: rl: detected multiple active sessions for token ghp4f8a9 within 60s window; session_ids: [sess-541, sess-542]; aggregated_tokens: 552; policy: per-connection accounting enabled

ryan_sre: FYI — we pushed a change last month to start per-connection accounting to make per-connection throttles stricter (helps noisy-tenant isolation). That might cause this behavior where quick reconnects double-count. We intended to later add a session de-dup window, but it wasn't enabled for hosted yet.

alex_support: OK — action items: (1) Provide sample logs (we'll need the server logs for req_0A1B2C and the internal session ids), (2) we'll open an internal ticket to evaluate short-term billing adjustment for the customer if we confirm duplicate counts, (3) engineering to evaluate enabling session de-dup or treating immediate reconnects as continuation (tunable).

sam_customer: thanks — attaching server logs via DM now. We need a quick mitigation; customers are upset because their quotas burned twice.

maria_eng: Received logs. Quick repro we ran locally: start SSE, inject a 429 mid-stream, client reconnects with same token. We see our meter create a second session entry before the first session finalizer runs. Repro snippet from our side: 
```
[2025-03-14T15:12:42Z] req=req_0A1B2C session=sess-541 state=streaming tokens=432
[2025-03-14T15:12:42Z] req=req_0A1B2C session=sess-541 event=rate_limit code=429
[2025-03-14T15:12:43Z] req=req_0A1B2C session=sess-542 new_connection detected (same token) tokens=120
[2025-03-14T15:12:44Z] session_finalizer sess-541 triggered (timeout) billed_tokens=432
[2025-03-14T15:12:44Z] session_finalizer sess-542 triggered billed_tokens=120
```

maria_eng: So it is double-billing because finalizer billed both sessions separately. Two options: quick config change to extend finalizer grace window (so reconnections within X seconds merge) or short-term billing credit.

ryan_sre: I'll flip the grace window to 5s for hosted accounts as a rollback-safe change. That should make immediate reconnections merge into the prior session and avoid double-counting. Deploying now to canary.

alex_support: I'll start a billing ticket to review charges and propose a credit for affected customers. Sam, can you provide a list of affected user ids and approximate totals?

sam_customer: Sent a CSV in DM with user ids and timestamps. Totals per user included. We appreciate the quick follow-up.

maria_eng: Canary shows expected behavior: reconnection within 5s merges tokens into sess-541 and session_finalizer only bills once. We'll monitor for 1h and then roll to prod if stable.

alex_support: Closing the loop: created support case #SUP-2247 and billing case #BILL-891. We'll notify after production rollout and final credit decision.

sam_customer: Awesome — thanks everyone. Small follow-up: could you add guidance to our docs about using a session_id header (X-Session-Id) or explicit resume token so clients can avoid transient reconnects duplicating work?

maria_eng: Good call. We'll add a docs note and recommend adding X-Session-Id or using short-lived resume tokens.

alex_support: Marking this thread resolved for now; re-open if you see further duplicates after prod rollout. :thumbsup:
